question.problem: Given the curve $r(t)=({t}^{2}-8)\,i-4t\,j$, find all of the points at which ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $r(t)$ are perpendicular.
question.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-8)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-4t)\,j \\  & =2t\,i-4\,j\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors $r(t)$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are perpendicular for some value of the parameter $t$ if and only if $r(t)\cdot {r}^{′}(t)=0.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t)\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =0 \\ [({t}^{2}-8)\,i-4t\,j]\cdot (2t\,i-4\,j) & =0 \\ ({t}^{2}-8)\cdot 2t+(-4t)\cdot (-4) & =0 \\ 2{t}^{3}-16t+16t & =0 \\ 2{t}^{3} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the only solution is $t=0.$

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0)=({0}^{2}-8)\,i-4(0)\,j=-8i,\end{aligned}
$$

 we conclude that $r(t)$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are perpendicular at the point $(-8,0).$
